summary: TypeScript SDK missing Authorization header in edge runtime during streaming
description: Issue summary: Customer sees 403 Forbidden when calling streaming chat completions from a Next.js Edge Runtime using redwood-sdk-typescript v1.4.0. Non-streaming calls sometimes work; curl works consistently. Impact: partial outage for end-user feature behind streaming endpoint. Steps: (1) Next.js Edge route handler (2) create client with apiKey (3) call chat.completions.stream() (4) request fails with 403; headers in their proxy logs show Authorization missing. Notes: likely a fetch/Headers serialization issue in edge runtime.
comments: Chloe Martin (Support): Customer provided HAR + proxy logs showing no Authorization header on failed requests.

Dev Patel (DevEx): We use undici in node; Edge uses global fetch. There is a code path that builds Headers from a plain object and may drop 'authorization' when value is undefined (race with async key load).
Customer (Hearthside): apiKey is set; we confirmed it logs correctly. Only streaming path fails.
Dev Patel: Found bug: streaming helper constructs request init twice and overwrites headers; the second init loses Authorization in edge environment due to Headers merge semantics.
Chloe Martin: Workaround: pass explicit headers in request options; confirmed by customer.
Dev Patel: Fix shipped in v1.4.1; customer confirmed 200 OK and streaming stable.
